items.look_for: F1 'snowy region': 256 tiles of 16x32 in a 16x16 grid. Rows 1-4 = 'wild' (blocks 320, shared by every outdoor region: grass, trees, water, paths), rows 5-8 = 'palace' (480), rows 9-12 = 'swamp' (520), rows 13-16 = 'mountain2' (560). Every tile should be a clean, unstriped 16x32 image; colour 31 is the default light blue.
items.title: Region 0 (F1) — snowy region

items.look_for: F2 'witch wood': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'build' (360, village buildings), rows 9-12 'rock' (400), rows 13-16 'tower' (440). Same four groups as region 3 (F4), so the two atlases are identical by source.
items.title: Region 1 (F2) — witch wood

items.look_for: F3 'swampy region': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'build' (360), rows 9-12 'swamp' (520), rows 13-16 'mountain2' (560). Rows 1-4 match region 0; rows 5-8 match region 1; rows 9-16 match region 0.
items.title: Region 2 (F3) — swampy region

items.look_for: F4 'plains and rocks': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'build' (360), rows 9-12 'rock' (400), rows 13-16 'tower' (440). Identical to region 1 (F2) by source (same image blocks).
items.title: Region 3 (F4) — plains and rocks

items.look_for: F5 'desert area': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'palace' (480), rows 9-12 'swamp' (520), rows 13-16 'mountain3' (600). In the RGBA atlas every pixel of palette index 31 is the desert override 0x0980 (dark sandy yellow) instead of the default light blue — compare with region 0 rows 1-4, which share the same 'wild' tiles.
items.title: Region 4 (F5) — desert area (colour 31 = 0x0980)

items.look_for: F6 'bay / city / farms': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'castle' (280), rows 9-12 'field' (240, farmland), rows 13-16 'mountain1' (200). Same four groups as region 7 (F8), so the two atlases are identical by source.
items.title: Region 5 (F6) — bay / city / farms

items.look_for: F7 'volcanic': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'doom' (640, the only region using this group), rows 9-12 'swamp' (520), rows 13-16 'mountain3' (600).
items.title: Region 6 (F7) — volcanic

items.look_for: F8 'forest and wilderness': rows 1-4 'wild' (320), rows 5-8 'castle' (280), rows 9-12 'field' (240), rows 13-16 'mountain1' (200); identical to region 5 (F6). Good atlas for the highlight mask: set bits (indices 16-24, the entries fade_page night-boosts) should sit on the green foliage and blue water pixels, not on paths or buildings.
items.title: Region 7 (F8) — forest and wilderness

items.look_for: F9 'inside of buildings': rows 1-4 'under' (680), rows 5-8 'furnish' (720, furniture), rows 9-12 'inside' (800, interior walls/floors), rows 13-16 'astral' (840). No outdoor 'wild' tiles here.
items.title: Region 8 (F9) — inside of buildings

items.look_for: F10 'dungeons and caves': rows 1-4 'under' (680), rows 5-8 'cave' (760, the only region using this group), rows 9-12 'inside' (800), rows 13-16 'astral' (840). In the RGBA atlas palette index 31 is the dungeon override 0x0445 (dark blue-grey) instead of light blue — compare rows 1-4 and 9-16 with region 8, which share those tiles. (The secret_timer variant 0x00f0 is not rendered.)
items.title: Region 9 (F10) — dungeons and caves (colour 31 = 0x0445)

T2.2.summary: One background tile atlas per region (file_index[0..9] = F1..F10): 256 tiles of 16x32 px in a 16-column grid, decoded from the four 40-block image groups each region loads (rows 1-4 = group 0, 5-8 = group 1, 9-12 = group 2, 13-16 = group 3). Check the RGBA atlas is recognizable terrain (not garbage/striped), the indexed twin shows the same imagery, and the highlight mask (palette 16-24) sits on vegetation/water pixels. Regions 4 and 9 render palette index 31 with their fade_page override colour.
T2.2.title: Background tiles
